title: BLOOD SIMPLE (1984)
location: DeBartolo Performing Arts Center, 100 Performing Arts Center | Notre Dame, 46556
description: Crime, Blood, and Laughs: The Coen Brothers Directed by Joel Coen With John Getz, Frances McDormand, Dan Hedaya Rated R, 96 minutes, Blu-ray This razor-sharp modern film noir, the first film by Joel and Ethan Coen, introduced the brothers' inimitable black humor and eccentric sense of character, a sensibility that has helped shape the course of contemporary American cinema. Deep in the heart of Texas, a sleazy bar owner suspects his wife of having an affair and hires a private detective to confirm his suspicions—only to have the crosshairs turned back on himself. Playfully shot by Barry Sonnenfeld and featuring a haunting score by Carter Burwell and a cunning performance by Frances McDormand, Blood Simple was a career-launching film for this ensemble and the first articulation of the precision of style that has defined the Coens' work ever since. Sponsored by the Meg and John P. Brogan Endowment for Classic Cinema.

title: JOSH ROUSE WSG THE SANCHEZ AGENCY TRIO
location: Stockroom East | 625 E Jefferson Blvd | South Bend, IN 46617
description:
With brill building wit and a Midwestern sense of melancholy, Josh Rouse has built a career that spans over 25 years, reaching back to his acclaimed 1998 debut Dressed Up Like Nebraska & continuing to his breakthrough albums 1972 & Nashville. His well-crafted and hook-laden tracks are coupled with closely-detailed, well-observed vignettes in his lyrics. Now passing 50, Josh faces the next phase of his life. “I remember seeing Tom Waits on the cover of a magazine with the headline TOM WAITS AT 50.” Josh recalls “ I was in my twenties and that seemed so far off… but he made a great record (Mule Variations) and I hope I have, too.”

As Rouse drifts into middle age, his worldview has expanded – family, travel… life, which adds even more depth to the songs. Paste Magazine has lauded Rouse, saying, “His knack for setting a simple feeling to a breezy melody shines through again and again,” and this is once again true with his latest album Going Places. So we see the laconic “She’s in L.A.,” the crisp and snappy “The Lonely Postman,” drenched in almost-Buddy Holly-esque melodies, and album closer “Stick Around” punctuated by its punching horn touches, a nod to his return to Tennessee and the city’s country-soul history.

title: LITTLE WOMEN (2019)
location: DeBartolo Performing Arts Center, 100 Performing Arts Center | Notre Dame, 46556
description: Browning Cinema Professor Pfinklepfunder's $1 Sunday Films Directed by Greta Gerwig With Saoirse Ronan, Emma Watson, Florence Pugh Rated PG, 135 minutes, Blu-ray The four March sisters have been part of American libraries and reading nooks for almost as long as the University of Notre Dame has been around. Louisa May Alcott's timeless band of sisters has been adapted for film previously, but perhaps never with as much panache or splash as when Greta Gerwig (director of Barbie) released this film as the pandemic was dawning. Meg (Emma Watson) , Jo (Saoirse Ronan) , Beth (Eliza Scanlen) , and Amy (Florence Pugh) experience the many seasons of New England life, including the rivalries, heartbreaks, and joys that come with such a warm home. Sponsored by the Meg and John P. Brogan Endowment for Classic Cinema.

title: SAMSARA (2011)
location: DeBartolo Performing Arts Center, 100 Performing Arts Center | Notre Dame, 46556
description: GET TICKETSBrowning Cinema Sunday Docs Directed by Ron Fricke With Puti Sri Candra Dewi, Marcos Luna, Kikumaru Rated PG-13, 102 minutes, DCP With Samsara, filmmaker Ron Fricke continues the legacy of the Qatsi trilogy by creating a global travelogue with pictures and music, exploring the Himalayas, the American Southwest, European cathedrals, and other beautiful sites. The focus here is the Poetic Documentary, which is a classification of films that rely less on linear continuity used to create narratives or storylines in films depicting reality. Often lushly shot, the editing of this slice of documentaries pushes for emotional experiences as opposed to the more educational approaches taken by other styles. Sponsored by the Meg and John P. Brogan Endowment for Documentary Film.

title: THE CHRISTOPHERS (2025)
location: DeBartolo Performing Arts Center, 100 Performing Arts Center | Notre Dame, 46556
description: Browning Cinema New at the Browning Directed by Steven Soderbergh With Ian McKellen, Michaela Coel, James Corden Rated R, 100 minutes, DCP Steven Soderbergh and Ian McKellen, two guys with zillions of credits to their filmographies, team up with the brilliant but lesser seen Miachaela Coel (I May Destroy You, Chewing Gum) in this lively black comedy. A mainstay of the London art scene since his starry breakout in the creative explosion of the 1960's, Julian Sklar (McKellen) has drifted into a cluttered, self-imposed seclusion. His two estranged children (James Corden, Jessica Gunning) enlist Lori (Coel) , a young painter and sometime-forger, to pose as a prospective assistant and gain access to a fabled series of unfinished canvases Julian has buried deep in his home studio, in a deceptive bid to secure an inheritance for themselves.
